claims.text: Standard laser powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys can produce residual stresses.
Standard laser powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys can produce porosity and micro-cracks.
Rapid solidification and incomplete interlayer bonding cause dimensional distortion and defects in laser-powder-bed-fused high-entropy alloys.
An in-situ laser remelting pass after every deposited layer will reduce residual stress.
An in-situ laser remelting pass after every deposited layer will heal fabrication-induced porosity.
An in-situ laser remelting pass after every deposited layer will heal fabrication-induced micro-cracks.
In-situ laser remelting will improve the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
In-situ laser remelting will improve the overall mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Local remelting and resolidification refine the grain structure.
Local remelting and resolidification reduce residual-stress gradients responsible for dimensional distortion.
Surface-tension-driven liquid flow during remelting eliminates voids.
Surface-tension-driven liquid flow during remelting improves interlayer fusion.
Controlled resolidification after remelting relieves thermal stresses.
Excessive remelting heat input can coarsen the microstructure.
Moderate substrate preheating can aid remelting without overheating the material.
Compared with baseline laser powder bed fusion, in-situ remelting will reduce dimensional deviation.
Compared with baseline laser powder bed fusion, in-situ remelting will increase tensile strength.
Compared with baseline laser powder bed fusion, in-situ remelting will improve ductility.
The predicted dimensional and mechanical improvements result from lower defect density and a more homogeneous microstructure.
The effectiveness of remelting may depend on alloy composition, part size, process scale, and thermal properties.
